agents.activatesWhen: A playable scene exists with at least one gameplay event worth scoring
agents.purpose: Decides what the game sounds like and which moments earn sound at all, then judges delivered audio against that.
agents.existsBecause: In a game where dozens of enemies die per minute, sounding every event produces noise rather than feedback. Deciding what stays silent is the central audio judgement and it belongs to one owner.
measurableOutput: Audio direction stating the sonic palette and which events are deliberately silent
Accept or reject decisions on delivered audio against that direction
agents.successMetric: Gameplay moments where simultaneous sounds mask the one the player needs. Target: zero.
mustEscalate: Audio requires a purchase or licence
The direction conflicts with the art direction

agents.activatesWhen: An audio direction has been recorded
agents.purpose: Writes the specification for each sound effect: what it signals, its length, frequency character and how often it may repeat.
agents.existsBecause: A sound effect in a survivor game plays hundreds of times per session, so repetition tolerance and frequency placement are engineering constraints rather than taste. Whoever eventually makes the sound needs those numbers.
measurableOutput: Per-effect sound specifications with duration, frequency band and repetition tolerance
Variation requirements for effects that repeat frequently
agents.successMetric: Shipped effects that become fatiguing within a single session. Target: zero.
mustEscalate: Two effects need the same frequency band
An event has no distinguishable sound available

agents.activatesWhen: A run has distinguishable intensity phases
agents.purpose: Specifies the music: layers, intensity transitions, loop structure and how it responds to run state.
agents.existsBecause: Music in a run-based game is adaptive rather than linear, which makes it a systems specification — layers, transition points, loop seams — quite unlike specifying a sound effect.
measurableOutput: Adaptive music specification with layers and intensity transition triggers
Loop structure requirements with seam constraints
agents.successMetric: Audible seams or abrupt transitions in shipped music. Target: zero.
mustEscalate: Run state does not expose the intensity signal needed
Music budget cannot hold the layer count

agents.activatesWhen: Audio has been wired into a playable scene
agents.purpose: Verifies that what was specified is what actually plays: every event fires, nothing clips, voice counts stay bounded.
agents.existsBecause: Audio integration fails silently — a trigger that never fires produces no error, just absence. The engineer who wired it is the wrong party to confirm it, and no other test covers sound.
measurableOutput: Per-event verification that the specified sound fires under the specified condition
Clipping and voice-count measurements under sustained load
agents.successMetric: Specified audio events that never fire in play. Target: zero.
mustEscalate: An event cannot be triggered in play
mayNot: Pass an event that does not fire
